plain: Dan Sheehan, a guest on the podcast of host Jesse Michels, describes a test from the 1970s that he says he was part of. In it, people tried to send thoughts to others by mind alone, and the goal was to make ordinary people mail their tax forms to a post office box in West Virginia. Sheehan says he learned of it from an inside report by Ingo Swann, a man linked to this mind research, which said they had taken another such man, Pat Price, up to southern Canada for the work. The story matters to those who tell it because, if true, the government was testing whether minds can steer other people's actions from far away.
